chunks: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to me from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, who said: Ibrahim ibn Ishaq narrated to me from Muhammad ibn Sulayman al-Daylami from his father from Qays, the seller of al-Zutti, who said:

I entered upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and said to him, 'May I be your ransom, I have a neighbor whom I notice only by his voice, either reciting a book and concluding it, or glorifying Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.' He said, 'Unless he be a Nassibi (one who bears enmity to the Ahl al-Bayt).' So I inquired about him in secret and in public, and it was said to me, 'He is one who gathers the prohibitions.'

He said, 'O Maisarah, he knows something of what you are upon.' I said, 'Allah knows best.' So I performed Hajj the following year and inquired about the man, and found that he knew nothing of this matter. So I entered upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and informed him of the man's news. He said to me, 'Like what he said in the past year: he knows something of what you are upon.' I said, 'No.'
He said, 'O Maisarah, which of the lands has the greatest sanctity?' I said, 'Allah and His Messenger and the Son of His Messenger know best.'

He said, 'O Maisarah, between the Rukn and the Maqaam is a garden from the gardens of Paradise. And by Allah, if a servant whom Allah prolongs the life of prays between the Rukn and the Maqaam for one thousand years, and between the Grave and the Pulpit worships for one thousand years, then is slaughtered on his bed wrongfully as the black sheep is slaughtered, and then meets Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, without our Wilayah, it is incumbent upon Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, to cast him headlong onto his nostrils in the Fire of Hell.'

key_terms.الرُّکْن: The Rukn (a pillar of the Kaaba)
key_terms.الْمَقَام: The Maqaam (the stone where Prophet Ibrahim stood)
key_terms.نَاصِبِیّاً: One who bears enmity to the Ahl al-Bayt

ai.seo_question: What is the condition for acceptance of worship according to this hadith?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq records this narration to emphasize that Wilayah is the essential condition for the acceptance of all acts of worship, illustrating the Shia doctrine that ritual piety without allegiance to the Ahl al-Bayt is ultimately futile. The Imam’s vivid imagery of a person being cast headlong into Hell despite a thousand years of devotion between the Rukn and Maqaam underscores the gravity of denying Imamate, a core tenet distinguishing Shia theology from other schools.
